texts.preamble: M/S Rameshwaram Transport vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 November, 2021
texts.facts: The petitioner is aggrieved by the order dated 13.02.2019 (Anneuxre P-12), issued by the Managing Director, M.P. State Civil Supplies Corporation Limited (hereinafter referred to as 'the Corporation') blacklisting it for a period of 10 years for alleged irregularity pointed therein. 2. The petitioner, entered into an agreement with respondent on 01.09.2015, for a duration till 30.06.2017, for transportation of grains to the lead societies under the Shahpura District Centre from godowns under 'Dwar Praday Yojana of year 2017'. The petitioner was served with an order of termination-cum-blacklisting dated 14.06.2016, debarring it from participating in future bids for 10 years by invoking clause 40 of the terms and conditions of NIT. It was suspected that the petitioner has used forged receipts and the grains were transported and black-marketed at other than destined sector. 3. Petitioner assailed the aforesaid order by way of W.P. No.12878/2016, on the ground that the order impugned was passed without affording opportunity of hearing, thereby violating the principles of natural justice and has caused a great prejudice to the petitioner preventing him from M/S Rameshwaram Transport vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 November, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57735395/ 1 participating in similar tenders. Taking note of the fact that the impugned order dated 14.06.2016 was a termination-cum-blacklisting order, the petition was directed to be entertained only on the issue as to blacklisting the petitioner, whereas, against the termination of contract, the petitioner was set at liberty to pursue the remedy of arbitration. The writ petition was finally disposed of vide order 26.09.2016 and the order of blacklisting was [LEAKAGE_MASK]. The matter was relegated to the competent authority to pass fresh orders on blacklisting after affording an opportunity of hearing to the petitioner. It was further observed that, "this remand order will not create any right in the petitioner to claim fresh contract or the continuation of the existing contract. The reasons being that, the allegation against the petitioner are serious enough for the respondent corporation to exercise its discretion till the petitioner is cleared of and exonerated of the allegation." 4. It is a matter of record that a Writ Appeal bearing No.764/2016 was thereafter preferred for expunging the said observation. The same, however, came to be withdrawn on 03.10.2017 with liberty to challenge the subsequent order dated 21.11.2016 passed by the competent authority, pursuant to order dated 26.09.2016. The order of detention was challenged by way of W.P. No.19671/2016, which came to be dismissed on 08.05.2017. It is a matter of record that after dismissal of the writ petition, an application for reconsideration was preferred before the Ministry of Home and Internal Affairs, whereupon a detailed report from the Collector/District Magistrate, Jabalpur as well as from the District Manager of the Corporation was called for in regard to the illegalities committed. The Statement of shop owners of concerned fair price shops were also got recorded by the authorities, who verified the fact that food grains were duly supplied to the different fair price shops. In view of these subsequent evidence and reports, petitioner preferred a R.P. No.1277/2017 for recalling the order dated 08.05.2017. The review petition was allowed and the order of detention dated 11.07.2016 was [LEAKAGE_MASK]. 6. In the light of these subsequent documents/evidence and letters dated 08.09.2017 and 08.01.2018, forwarded by respondent No.3 to respondent No.2 to withdraw/cancel the order of blacklisting, the petitioner submitted a fresh representation before the authorities for reconsideration of his case, which unfortunately, remained pending. The petitioner thereafter preferred W.P. No.25551/2018, which was disposed of on 12.12.2018 with a direction to the authority to decide the pending representation in the light of order passed in R.P. No.1277/2017 and in view of the official communication dated 08.01.2018. In pursuant to the same, the respondent No.1 rejected the representation of the petitioner, which has led to filing of present petition.
texts.arguments: 7. Shri Sankalp Kochar, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner submitted that the impugned order is arbitrary, illegal and contrary to the directions given by this Court in W.P. No. 25551/2018. Referring to clause 40.2 of the NIT and the communication dated 08.09.2017 and 08.01.2018, it is urged that clause 40.2 envisages imposition of penalty of blacklisting under the recommendation of the District Manager and concerned Regional Manager of the Corporation, however, in the present M/S Rameshwaram Transport vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 November, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57735395/ 2 case the District Manager himself has recommended for withdrawal/cancellation of the order of blacklisting. It is further submitted that the directions of this Court and also the subsequent report and the statements of the shop keepers, though brought to the notice of competent authority were deliberately ignored and overlooked and his representation was dismissed with malafide intent, holding that the petitioner has failed to bring any new facts or evidence on record. 8. It is argued on behalf of respondents No.2 and 3/Corporation that the concerned clause 26 of NIT clearly stated that only authorized vehicles will be used for transportation under the scheme, and any other vehicle could only be used for the purpose of transportation with the prior sanction/permission of Corporation or Collector. Petitioner, however, without any such permission used the vehicles which were not authorized/ mentioned in the agreement. He further contended that in the preliminary investigation, it was found that the food grains were never supplied to the fair price shop and the same were misappropriated for which the answering respondent has duly invoked clause 40.2 of the contract and imposing the penalty for blacklisting against the petitioner. 11. The effect of blacklisting has been high lighted by Supreme Court in the case of (2021) 2 SCC 551 UMC Technologies Private Limited Vs. Food Corporation of India and another, held thus :- "14. Specifically, in the context of blacklisting of a person or an entity by the state or a state corporation, the requirement of a valid, particularized and unambiguous show cause notice is particularly crucial due to the severe consequences of blacklisting and the stigmatization that accrues to the person/entity being blacklisted. Here, it may be gainful to describe the concept of blacklisting and the graveness of the consequences occasioned by it. Blacklisting has the effect of denying a person or an entity the privileged opportunity of entering into government contracts. This privilege arises because it is the State who is the counterparty in government contracts and as such, every eligible person is to be afforded an equal opportunity to participate in such contracts, without arbitrariness and discrimination. Not only does blacklisting takes away this privilege, it also tarnishes the blacklisted person's reputation and brings the person's character into question. Blacklisting also has long-lasting civil consequences for the future business prospects of the blacklisted person." 12. In Kulja Industries Limited Vs. Chief General Manager, Western Telecom Project Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited and others (2014) 14 SCC 731, while referring to the passage from the decision in Mahabir Auto Stores Vs. Indian Oil Corporation (1990) 3 SCC 752, the Supreme Court has held :- M/S Rameshwaram Transport vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 November, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57735395/ 3 "20. It is also well settled that even though the right of the writ petitioner is in the nature of a contractual right, the manner, the method and the motive behind the decision of the authority whether or not to enter into a contract is subject to judicial review on the touchstone of fairness, relevance, natural justice, non-discrimination, equality and proportionality. All these considerations that go to determine whether the action is sustainable in law have been sanctified by judicial pronouncements of this Court and are of seminal importance in a system that is committed to the rule of law. We do not consider it necessary to burden this judgment by a copious reference to the decisions on the subject. A reference to the following passage from the decision of this Court in M/s Mahabir Auto Stores & Ors. v. Indian Oil Corporation Ltd., (1990) 3 SCC 752 should, in our view, suffice: "12. It is well settled that every action of the State or an instrumentality of the State in exercise of its executive power, must be informed by reason. In appropriate cases, actions uninformed by reason may be questioned as arbitrary in proceedings under Article 226 or Article 32 of the Con- situation. Reliance in this connection may be placed on the observations of this Court in M/s Radha Krishna Agarwal & Ors. v. State of Bihar & Ors., [1977] 3 SCC 457 ..... In case any right conferred on the citizens which is sought to be interfered, such action is subject to Article 14 of the Constitution, and must be reasonable ..... It appears to us that rule of reason and rule against arbitrariness and discrimination, rules of fair play and natural justice are part of the rule of law applicable in situation or action by State instrumentality in dealing with citizens in a situation like the present one. Even though the rights of the citizens are in the nature of contractual rights, the manner, the method and motive of a decision of entering or not entering into a contract, are subject to judicial review on the touchstone of relevance and reasonableness, fair play, natural justice, equality and non-discrimination in the type of the transactions and nature of the dealing as in the present case." 13. In Erusian Equipment and Chemicals Limited Vs. State of West Bengal (1975) 1 SCC 70, the Supreme Court has held:- 17. The Government is a Government of laws and not of men. It is true that neither the petitioner nor the respondent has any right to enter into a contract but they are entitled to equal treatment with others who offer tender or quotations for the purchase of the goods. This privilege arises because it is the Government which is trading with the public and the democratic form of Government demands equality and absence of arbitrariness and discrimination in such transactions. Hohfeld treats privileges as a form of liberty as opposed to a duty. The activities of the Government have a public element and, therefore, there should be fairness and equality. The State need not enter into any contract with any one but if it does so, it must do so fairly without discrimination and without unfair procedure. Reputation is a part of a person's character and personality. Blacklisting tarnishes one's reputation." M/S Rameshwaram Transport vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 November, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57735395/ 4 14. The principles laid down in Erusian Equipment and Chemicals Limited (supra) has also been followed in Patel Engineering Limited Vs. Union of India (2012) 11 SCC 257, Daffodills Pharmaceuticals Limited and another Vs. State of U.P. and another 2019 SCC Online 1607, Medipol Pharmaceutical India Private Limited Vs. Post Graduate Institute of Medical Education and Research and another 2020 Online SC 638 and Vet India Pharmaceuticals Ltd. Vs. State of U.P. and another (2021) 1 SCC 804. 15. 22. I am not impressed with the arguments of Shri Shobhit Aditya, learned counsel for the Corporation that matter be remitted back to the authority for deciding the period for which M/S Rameshwaram Transport vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 9 November, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/57735395/ 7 petitioners should be blacklisted, having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case.
